name: AR-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Steve Womack seeking re-election with a large cash advantage
Democratic challenger Robb Ryerse raised only about $120K with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic win chances at roughly 6%
model.rationale: Northwest Arkansas's third district is firmly Republican, Womack is a well-funded incumbent with over $2.4 million on hand against a challenger who raised about $120K, and markets give Democrats only a small chance. The fundamentals and money gap point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: A late surge in challenger fundraising or a major scandal involving Womack would be needed to move this race toward competitive territory.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Arkansas's third district has been held by Republican Steve Womack since 2011 and carries a double-digit Republican lean in recent partisan performance. Womack enters the general election after easily securing renomination, with a large financial advantage: roughly $2.4 million on hand compared with about $6,000 for Democratic challenger Robb Ryerse, who raised around $120,000. A Libertarian candidate, Bobby Wilson, is also on the ballot but has shown little fundraising activity.

No public general-election polling is available for this race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 6% chance of an upset. The combination of the district's lean, Womack's incumbency, and the lopsided money race points to a comfortable Republican win, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
